_about: The forgiveness hub (plan 7.6f), built the way love and righteousness are: the rows are defined by the Hebrew and Greek, a verb row by who forgives and what, from the frames, or by hand where the frames are silent (the Hebrew passive 'he will be forgiven', Lev 4-6, has no frame at all), a noun row by the words standing in the noun's own phrase or verse, and a verse sits in every row it fits (match: all). The review panel flagged forgiveness HIGH (committee-flags.json): ἀφίημι also means 'leave, let go, permit' (so a sense rule keeps only the verses that render it forgive); who may forgive (God alone, the Son of Man, John 20:23), whether forgiveness is conditional on repentance, 'forgive us as we forgive', repentance and baptism (Acts 2:38), forgiveness and sacrifice. So those are set side by side, as the text has them, each with a note that the page takes no side, and no row orders repentance, baptism, faith and forgiveness or states a condition. Built by tools/concepts/hub_build.py into out/concept-hubs/forgiveness.json.

titles.noun: What the text says of forgiveness

_words_why: The card's own words: סָלַח (forgive, pardon -- said in every verse of the LORD, or passively 'he will be forgiven'), its nouns סְלִיחָה and סַלָּח, and ἀφίημι and ἄφεσις. נָשָׂא is mostly 'lift, carry, bear' (610 verses) and counts ONLY where the verse renders it forgive or pardon (20 verses: 'forgiving iniquity, transgression and sin', Exod 34:7; and asked of a person, Gen 50:17); the same sense rule drops ἀφίημι 'left', 'permit', 'let go' (the fever left her, Matt 8:15; Matt 19:14 'let the little children come') and ἄφεσις 'release' (Luke 4:18, rendered 'deliverance'). The Hebrew and the Greek are not pooled as one: every example names the word it stands on. כִּפֶּר (make atonement) is a different word and is NOT in the rows: it stands in the verses beside forgiveness in Lev 4-6 and Num 15 and the label of that row names both; its 8 verses the lexicon glosses forgive are under 'Other words the lexicon glosses forgive' with the other different words (χαρίζομαι, ἀπολύω). χαρίζομαι (Eph 4:32, Col 3:13, Col 2:13, 2 Cor 2:7-10) is 'to give graciously' and is likewise a different word that the English renders forgive.
_sense_why: 'forgiv' is forgive, forgiven, forgiving, forgiveness; 'forgave' is the past tense, which 'forgiv' does not match and which first dropped Matt 18:27 and 18:32 ('forgave his debt') and Ps 32:5, 85:2 (found 2026-10-10); 'pardon' is the Berean's rendering of סָלַח at Isa 55:7, Num 14:20 and of נָשָׂא at 1 Sam 15:25, Job 7:21. Num 30:5, 8, 12 (the LORD 'will absolve her' of a vow) are MACULA's glosses 'forgive' and stay.

others._why: Words the lexicon glosses 'forgive' that are not this concept's own (as love names φιλέω and חֶסֶד apart). Rule: a different word is named apart with its verses and never handed over as the same. כִּפֶּר 'make atonement' (8 of its 94 verses are glossed forgive; the Berean prints 'forgave' only at Ps 78:38 and 'atone', 'atoned for', 'provide atonement', 'wipe out' in the rest), χαρίζομαι 'give graciously' (the Berean prints forgive in all 8), ἀπολύω 'release' (Luke 6:37, 'Forgive, and you will be forgiven'). Panel fix 2026-10-10: retitled from 'translated forgive' (the gloss rule reads MACULA's gloss, not the Berean's English, so the title claimed more than the examples show); כָּסָה (Prov 17:9, Berean 'conceals an offense') and נָקָה (Joel 3:21, Berean 'avenge') are excluded because the Berean does not say forgive in either. 'add' (the builder's by-hand option, mercy panel 2026-10-10) puts the verses a reader should see first, each word with a note: without it the entry showed the first two by Bible order (Deut 21:8 and 2 Chr 30:18, 'atoned for' and 'provide atonement', for כִּפֶּר; Luke 7:42 and 2 Cor 12:13 for χαρίζομαι). כִּפֶּר leads with Ps 78:38 ('He forgave their iniquity') and Ps 79:9 ('atone for our sins'); χαρίζομαι with Eph 4:32 and Col 3:13, then Col 2:13 and 2 Cor 2:10. A filter of the verses themselves by the Berean's English is still not possible; the notes say it instead.

h3722.note: כִּפֶּר means “make atonement”, a different word from סָלַח. The Berean prints “forgave” here (Ps 78:38) and in no other of the eight verses the lexicon glosses forgive; elsewhere it prints “atone”, “atoned for”, “provide atonement” (Ps 65:3, Ps 79:9, Deut 21:8, 2 Chr 30:18). The page does not make the two words one.

g5483.note: χαρίζομαι means “give freely, grant”; the Berean prints “forgive” in these verses, and elsewhere “granted” and “freely give” (Phil 1:29; Rom 8:32; Gal 3:18). It is a different word from ἀφίημι, so these verses are not in the rows.

others.title: Other words the lexicon glosses “forgive”

_review: Not yet reviewed. The panel's flag (high): remove the verses where ἀφίημι does not mean forgive (sense rule, above); keep rows by who forgives and what is forgiven as written; set 'repentance for the forgiveness of sins', 'forgive us as we forgive' and John 20:23 side by side without ordering them or stating a condition. Taken so: the three contested sets are rows of their own (repentance, baptism and faith are three rows in the noun form, in the alphabetical order of their labels and each with the same no-side sentence, and the verb form has its faith and repentance rows in the same alphabetical order; the first panel said the order read as a ranking, and the notes now say what it is); 'Who can forgive sins' holds Mark 2:7, Mark 2:10 and John 20:23 together and ranks none above another; 'Forgive us as we forgive' is a row of its own, apart from the row of people forgiving one another. The divine persons are by hand: a row whose label names God, the LORD, the Father or the Holy Spirit is filled with verses where the verse itself names him; verses that say only 'He', 'I' or 'You' are a row of their own, with a note.

rows.label: The LORD, God, the Father forgives
rows.note: The verses where the text itself names the LORD, God or the Father as the one who forgives. In none of its 45 verses is the Hebrew סָלַח said of a person: its forgiver is the LORD, or the verb is passive (“he will be forgiven”). The Greek ἀφίημι is said also of people, in the rows below.
rows._why: by hand, as the divine persons are: a rule on 'the LORD' or θεός would take every verse near a name. Each verse names him: Num 14:20 'the LORD replied', Mic 7:18 'a God like You', Matt 6:14 'your heavenly Father', Isa 55:7 'the LORD ... our God', Num 14:18 'The LORD', Ps 99:8 'O LORD our God', Jer 31:34 'declares the LORD', Jer 50:20 'declares the LORD', Matt 6:15 'your Father', Mark 11:25 'your Father in heaven'. Acts 8:22 'pray to the Lord ... He will forgive' is left to the repentance row: 'the Lord' there is read of Jesus or of God and the page does not choose.

rows.label: “He forgives”, “I will forgive”, “You forgave”
rows.note: The verses say “He”, “I” or “You” and do not name who. In the Hebrew verses the passage around them names the LORD as the one spoken of, speaking or addressed (Exod 34:6; Ps 103:1; Ps 85:1; Num 14:17; Jer 5:9, 33:2, 36:1; 2 Chr 7:12); in 1 John 1:9 readers take “He” of the Father or of Christ, and the page does not choose.
rows._why: by hand, as the divine persons are (the 'He is righteous' row in righteousness): the text says only a pronoun. Ps 32:5, 85:2 and Num 14:19 are 'You forgave', addressed to the LORD (Lam 3:42, 'You have not forgiven', is the opposite and stands under 'Will not forgive')

rows.label: Asked in prayer: forgive
rows._why: by hand: the request itself (a command or a 'may You') made of the LORD or of the Father: Solomon's dedication (1 Kgs 8; 2 Chr 6), Daniel, Amos, Moses, Job, the Lord's Prayer (Matt 6:12; Luke 11:4) and Luke 23:34 ('Father, forgive them'). Ps 25:18 is in the glosses but the Berean reads 'take away all my sins' and it stays in 'Every other use'. Isa 2:9 ('do not forgive them') is the opposite request and stands under 'Not forgiven'

rows.label: Who can forgive sins
rows.note: Set side by side as the text has them: “Who can forgive sins but God alone?” (Mark 2:7; Luke 5:21; Luke 7:49), the Son of Man has authority on earth to forgive sins (Matt 9:6; Mark 2:10; Luke 5:24), “If you forgive anyone his sins, they are forgiven; if you withhold forgiveness from anyone, it is withheld” (John 20:23). Where traditions part on who may forgive, and how, the page takes no side and ranks none above another.
rows._why: by hand: the contested set the panel named (God alone; Jesus; the disciples/priestly absolution). The first four examples are one of each reading and the page orders none above another

rows.label: “Blessed are they whose sins are forgiven”; “Your sins are forgiven”
rows.note: The blessing of Psalm 32:1, which Romans 4:7 quotes; and the saying as the text gives it: Jesus to the paralytic and to the woman who anointed him, and John to little children (“through His name”). The text says the sins are forgiven and does not say here who forgives; “Who can forgive sins” is the row above.
rows._why: by hand. Merged 2026-10-10 from two rows ('Your sins are forgiven', 9; 'Blessed are those whose sins are forgiven', 2): both are the passive 'sins are forgiven' with no agent. Ps 32:1 has no frame (the Hebrew passive) and Rom 4:7 quotes it

rows.label: People forgiving people, and asked to
rows.note: People forgiving people: “forgive my brother”, “if your brother ... repents, forgive him” (Matthew 18; Luke 17), the master who “forgave his debt” (Matt 18:27, 32), and, in the Hebrew, a person asked to forgive (Joseph, Moses, Samuel, David) with נָשָׂא, not סָלַח (said only of the LORD). Eph 4:32 (“forgiving each other just as in Christ God forgave you”) and Col 3:13 use a different Greek word, χαρίζομαι, and Luke 6:37 (“Forgive, and you will be forgiven”) another, ἀπολύω; they are listed under “Other words the lexicon glosses forgive”, not here. The verses that join our forgiving to God's are the next row.
rows._why: by hand: Matt 6:12, 6:14, 6:15, Mark 11:25 and Luke 11:4 stand here too, as people forgiving, and in the next row. Merged 2026-10-10 from 'Asked of a person, or told to forgive one another' (13) and 'Debts forgiven' (3: Matt 6:12, 18:27, 18:32): the parable's master forgiving a servant is a person forgiving a person. Matt 6:12 'debts' stays visible in its verse

rows.label: Our forgiving, and our Father's
rows.note: The text's own phrases, set side by side and not ordered: “forgive us our debts, as we also have forgiven our debtors” (Matt 6:12; Luke 11:4), “if you forgive men their trespasses, your heavenly Father will also forgive you” (Matt 6:14-15; Mark 11:25), “unless you forgive your brother from your heart” (Matt 18:35). Whether, and in what sense, God's forgiveness depends on ours the page takes no side; whether our forgiving depends on the other's repenting is the question of Luke 17:3-4, in the row above. Eph 4:32 (“just as in Christ God forgave you”) and Col 3:13 (“Forgive as the Lord forgave you”) say the same of our forgiving in another Greek word, χαρίζομαι, and Luke 6:37 (“Forgive, and you will be forgiven”) in ἀπολύω; they are listed under “Other words the lexicon glosses forgive” below, and are kept out of the rows because they are different words.

rows.label: Forgiveness and faith
rows.note: “When Jesus saw their faith, He said ... your sins are forgiven” (Mark 2:5; Matt 9:2; Luke 5:20), “the prayer offered in faith ... If he has sinned, he will be forgiven” (Jas 5:15). The noun form has Acts 10:43 and 26:18. This row, the repentance row below and the baptism row in the noun form are listed in the alphabetical order of their labels and carry no ranking; where traditions part on how faith, repentance, baptism and forgiveness stand to one another, the page takes no side.

rows.label: Forgiveness, repentance, turning and confessing
rows.note: The verses that name repentance, turning or confessing in the verse itself: “humble themselves and pray ... turn from their wicked ways, then I will ... forgive” (2 Chr 7:14), “Let the wicked man forsake his way ... return to the LORD” (Isa 55:7), “if we confess our sins, He is faithful and just to forgive” (1 John 1:9), “if he repents, forgive him” (Luke 17:3), “turn and be forgiven” (Mark 4:12). Other verses name none in the verse (Luke 23:34; Luke 5:20; Ps 25:11). The page does not say whether forgiveness is conditional. This row, the faith row above and the baptism row in the noun form are listed in the alphabetical order of their labels and carry no ranking.
rows._why: by hand: a rule on שׁוּב takes verses where it means 'restore' or 'return' (1 Kgs 8:34 'restore them to the land'; 1 Sam 15:25 'return with me'; Neh 9:17 'return them to their bondage'), so each verse was read. Ps 32:5 'I acknowledged my sin to You ... I will confess my transgressions'

rows.label: Atonement made, and he will be forgiven
rows.note: The Hebrew has two words in these verses, כִּפֵּר “make atonement” and סָלַח “forgive”, side by side, and the page does not make them one; the atonement is made by the priest with the offering, the forgiving is said in the passive. The same כִּפֶּר is “atone” elsewhere (the Berean prints “atone”, “atoned for”, “provide atonement” at Ps 65:3, 79:9, Deut 21:8, 2 Chr 30:18) and “forgave” once (Ps 78:38); the page does not make the words one. Lev 6:2-7 gives this forgiveness after deceit, extortion and false swearing, wrongs done knowingly. How the offering and the forgiving are related is a question traditions answer differently, and the page takes no side.
rows._why: by hand: these verses have no frame at all (the Hebrew passive nisal), so no rule reaches them; each pairs כִּפֶּר with סָלַח

rows.label: Sinning unintentionally, in ignorance: forgiven
rows.note: These four verses say the sin was unintentional or in ignorance. Lev 6:2-7, in the atonement row above, has the same forgiving words for deceit, extortion and false swearing; Num 15:30-31 speaks of the person who sins defiantly, “cut off from among his people”, with no word for forgiveness. The page does not say what the text leaves unsaid.
rows._why: by hand (no frame, the Hebrew passive): 'the sin was unintentional' (Num 15:25), 'since it happened to all the people unintentionally' (Num 15:26, which has no word of atonement and so is not in the atonement row), 'sinning unintentionally' (Num 15:28), 'the wrong he has committed in ignorance' (Lev 5:18)

rows.label: Forgiving sins, iniquity, transgression, trespass

not_verses.Ps.25.18: the Berean reads 'take away all my sins' (the Hebrew verb is MACULA's 'forgive'); it stands under 'Every other use' where its own words show

rows._why: by the frames' patient, the text's own object of the verb; the label says only that these are what is forgiven or not (Josh 24:19 and Exod 23:21 'will not forgive' are here too, and also in 'Will not forgive')

rows.label: Will not forgive, was not forgiven
rows.note: Most are the LORD's refusal. Matt 6:15 sets it beside our not forgiving. Isa 2:9 is a plea that He not forgive. John 20:23 is said to the disciples and is set with Mark 2:7 and Mark 2:10 in “Who can forgive sins”, where the page takes no side.
rows._why: by hand: 'He will not forgive your rebellion' (Josh 24:19), 'The LORD will never be willing to forgive him' (Deut 29:20), 'the LORD was unwilling to forgive' (2 Kgs 24:4), 'he will not forgive rebellion' (Exod 23:21, of the angel), 'Why should I forgive you?' (Jer 5:7), 'do not forgive them' (Isa 2:9, a prayer), 'You have not forgiven' (Lam 3:42), Matt 6:15 and John 20:23 ('if you withhold forgiveness'). Hard verses stay

rows.label: Blasphemy against the Holy Spirit
rows.note: The verses set a word against the Son of Man (forgiven) beside blasphemy against the Spirit (not forgiven), and “all sins and blasphemies” forgiven men (Mark 3:28); Mark 3:29 is in the noun form. What the blasphemy is, readers take differently and the page takes no side.
rows._why: by hand: the Holy Spirit is a divine person and these four verses name him

rows.label: Every other use
rows.note: Numbers 30:5, 8, 12: the LORD “will absolve her” of a vow her father or husband has annulled -- the same Hebrew verb as in the rows above, a vow and not a sin. Psalm 25:18: the Berean reads “take away all my sins”; the Hebrew verb is the one the lexicon glosses forgive.
rows._why: the catch-all (consolidation 2026-10-10: 'The LORD will absolve her of a vow', 3, was folded in; Num 30:5, 8, 12 'the LORD will absolve her' when a father or husband nullifies a vow are MACULA's סָלַח 'forgive', a use of the word that is not forgiveness of sin, kept as written)

rows.label: With the LORD there is forgiveness
rows.note: Dan 9:9 sets forgiveness beside compassion, Neh 9:17 beside grace, compassion and loving devotion. The Hebrew speaks of sin taken away in other words, with no word for forgiveness, and those verses are not in this hub: “blots out your transgressions” (Isa 43:25), “As far as the east is from the west, so far has He removed our transgressions” (Ps 103:12), “cast out all our sins into the depths of the sea” (Mic 7:19), “blot out my transgressions” and “Wash me clean of my iniquity” (Ps 51:1-2).
rows._why: consolidation 2026-10-10: the row 'Forgiveness beside compassion, grace and loving devotion' (3: Dan 9:9, Neh 9:17, Eph 1:7) was folded in; its Hebrew two were already here, and Eph 1:7 ('the riches of His grace') stands in the phrase, blood and name rows. Panel fix 2026-10-10: moved to the first row of the noun form (the earliest verses on the noun, and the Hebrew heard first as in the verb form) and given the pointer to the Hebrew speech of sin taken away. By hand, Hebrew: 'But with You there is forgiveness' (Ps 130:4, addressed to the LORD of 130:1), 'To the Lord our God belong compassion and forgiveness' (Dan 9:9), 'You are a forgiving God' (Neh 9:17, in the prayer to the LORD of 9:6). The Greek ἄφεσις is not said 'with' anyone in the text; Acts 5:31 (God grants it) stands in the repentance row and the phrase row

rows.label: Forgiveness of sins, of trespasses
rows.note: Luke 1:77 sets it beside the knowledge of salvation, Eph 1:7 and Col 1:14 beside redemption, Acts 5:31 beside the Savior.
rows._why: consolidation 2026-10-10: the row 'Forgiveness, redemption and salvation' (4: Acts 5:31, Col 1:14, Eph 1:7, Luke 1:77) was a subset of this row (all four have ἁμαρτία or παράπτωμα next to ἄφεσις) and was folded into it; its doors came with it

rows.label: Baptism and forgiveness
rows.note: “A baptism of repentance for the forgiveness of sins” (Mark 1:4; Luke 3:3) is the baptism John preached; “Repent and be baptized, every one of you, in the name of Jesus Christ for the forgiveness of your sins” (Acts 2:38) is Peter's, at Pentecost. Acts 22:16 (“Get up, be baptized, and wash your sins away, calling on His name”) joins baptism and the washing away of sins without a word for forgiveness, and so is not in this hub. This row, the faith row below and the repentance row below it are in the alphabetical order of their labels and carry no ranking; where traditions part on what baptism does and how it stands to repentance, faith and forgiveness, the page takes no side.

rows.label: Believing, faith and forgiveness
rows.note: “Everyone who believes in Him receives forgiveness of sins through His name” (Acts 10:43), “forgiveness of sins and an inheritance among those sanctified by faith in Me” (Acts 26:18). This row sits between the baptism row above and the repentance row below in the alphabetical order of their labels and carries no ranking; the page takes no side on how they stand to one another.

rows.label: Repentance and forgiveness
rows.note: “Repentance and forgiveness of sins will be proclaimed” (Luke 24:47), “to grant repentance and forgiveness of sins to Israel” (Acts 5:31), “Repent and be baptized ... for the forgiveness of your sins” (Acts 2:38). The baptism, faith and repentance rows are in the alphabetical order of their labels and carry no ranking; where Christian traditions part on how repentance, baptism, faith and forgiveness stand to one another, the page takes no side.

rows.label: Blood, offering and forgiveness
rows.note: “Without the shedding of blood there is no forgiveness” (Heb 9:22), “My blood of the covenant, which is poured out for many for the forgiveness of sins” (Matt 26:28), “where these have been forgiven, an offering for sin is no longer needed” (Heb 10:18). Where traditions part on how Christ's blood and forgiveness are related, the page takes no side.

rows.label: Forgiveness “in His name”, “through Him”, “in Him”
rows.note: Acts 2:38 (“in the name of Jesus Christ”) and 13:38 (“through Jesus”) name Jesus in the verse; the others say “His name”, “Him”, “whom”, and the passage around them names Christ (Luke 24:46; Acts 10:36; Eph 1:5; Col 1:13). How the text relates Him to forgiveness -- by His name, through Him, in Him -- is in the verses, and the page does not choose.
rows._why: by hand, as the divine persons are. Acts 5:31 ('God exalted Him ... to grant repentance and forgiveness') and Matt 26:28 ('My blood') say 'Him' and 'My' without the phrase in the label and stand in their own rows

rows.label: Every other use
rows.note: Mark 3:29 (“will never be forgiven; he is guilty of eternal sin”): see “Blasphemy against the Holy Spirit” in the verb form, where Mark 3:28, Matt 12:31-32 and Luke 12:10 stand with it; what the blasphemy is, readers take differently and the page takes no side. The same noun ἄφεσις is also “release”: Luke 4:18 (“to proclaim liberty to the captives ... to release the oppressed”) is the one of its 16 verses where it is not forgiveness, and is not counted here.
